entry.title: Learning-To-Bound
entry.content:
Problem Definition & Notation

Let,

  • $\hat{\p}\brackets{\cdot}$ be any estimator that satisfies appropriate conditions.
  • $\bm{\epsilon}=\p-\hat{\p}\brackets{\X}$ the estimation error vector.

Then, given a dataset $\ds={\p_i,\x_i}_{i=1}^{\nds}$ of $\nds$ i.i.d parameter-measurement pairs, %$\ds$ of size $\nds$, lower bound the mean square error of $\hat{\p}\brackets{\cdot}$ by a learned bound $\matsym{LB}\brackets{\mathcal{D}}$, satisfying: \(\textbf{non-Bayesian: }\expectation{\vectorsym{\epsilon}\vectorsym{\epsilon}^T}{\X}&\succeq \matsym{B}\brackets{\p}\xleftarrow{\substack{\infty\leftarrow{}\nds}}\matsym{LB}\brackets{\p;\mathcal{D}}\quad \text{a.s},\) \(\textbf{Bayesian: }\expectation{\vectorsym{\epsilon}\vectorsym{\epsilon}^T}{\X,\p}&\succeq \matsym{B}\xleftarrow{\substack{\infty\leftarrow{}\nds}}\matsym{LB}\brackets{\mathcal{D}}\quad \text{a.s},\) where $\matsym{B}$ is the theoretical bound.

)

)

</details>)
